forces.title: Higher energy prices boost demand for efficient building products
forces.description: Rising energy costs significantly improve the economics for investments in insulation, high-performance glazing, and efficient heating systems by shortening their payback periods. This trend reinforces the value premium for energy-efficient homes, directly benefiting manufacturers and suppliers of these specific building products and materials within Belgium.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Stricter renovation standards drive demand for high-performance materials
forces.description: Increasingly stringent renovation requirements are making Belgian home buyers pay closer attention to future renovation costs, especially for poorly insulated properties. This encourages investments in energy-efficient materials like insulation and high-performance glazing, as energy performance becomes a critical determinant of a property's value and long-term marketability, representing a structural tailwind.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Strengthening construction activity fuels demand for building materials
forces.description: Irish construction activity continues to strengthen, with sustained new order inflows driving growth across commercial and civil engineering segments. Although housing remains the weakest area, strong underlying demand is expected to support long-term activity. This broad-based recovery in the construction sector directly translates into increased demand for various building products and materials in Ireland.

forces.title: Cost inflation, staff shortages, and delivery times challenge construction sector
forces.description: The Irish construction sector faces significant headwinds from persistent cost inflation, staff shortages, and lengthening delivery times. These factors increase operational costs and complexity for construction firms, potentially impacting their project pipelines, margins, and ultimately, the demand for or profitability of building products and materials used in construction projects.

viewpoints.title: Energy-efficient building materials demand resilient despite Belgian housing market cool-down
viewpoints.description: ING Think forecasts a gradual cooling in the Belgian housing market for 2026-2027, with nominal median house prices increasing by 2.5% and 2.0% respectively. Despite this overall slowdown, demand for energy-efficient homes is expected to remain resilient. Higher energy prices enhance the financial viability of investments in insulation and high-performance glazing by reducing their payback periods. Additionally, stricter renovation standards drive buyers to prioritize energy performance, making it a key factor in property value and marketability.
viewpoints.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

viewpoints.title: Irish construction recovery provides underlying support for building products demand
viewpoints.description: Allianz observes strengthening construction activity in Ireland, marked by a third consecutive month of growth driven by new order inflows across commercial and civil engineering. This broad-based recovery, alongside rising employment, suggests underlying momentum in the sector. Although housing remains the weakest segment due to policy constraints, strong fundamental demand is expected to support activity in the long term, creating a generally positive environment for the building products and materials sector.
